story: David hooked and reeled this one in himself!
Two at a time on a mackeral rig. 16 inches. Found them at Tinkers ledge off of Marblehead, MA.

Caught on an Irish jig at Tinker's ledge off of Marblehead, MA while targeting mackeral. I caught 5 of these guys in about 15 minutes. Note: they squirt ink, so beware when bringing one of these guys aboard! Very tasty when grilled with some olive oil and smoked paprika.
Trolling for white bass and snagged this monster. Managed to get him in on 10lb braid line with a 6lb leader.
Just trying to catch a bluegill to get the first fish of the year and caught this one instead.
Caught three walleye and this sauger from the same spot. It’s a back eddy on the other side of the river with a swift water channel to cast over. Caught on a Rapala suspending jerkbait.

Fishing with Kent on our birthday. Great day on the water catching Cod, Mackerel, and Pollock. Fishing in Kent's boat with Kent's fishing rod and Kent's lure. I probably should feel bad about breaking Kent's record.
Trolling for wipers with my friend Mike. Caught no wipers but did get a handfull of spotted bass with this one being the biggest.

Daredevil Pit is  a reclaimed surface mine with deep clear water. Caught this bluegill just off the bottom in 20 foot of water. Caught on a hand tied jig with blue rubber strand tail and olive brown chenile body.
Fishing for smallmouth and caught this one on a  Zoom tiny brush hog.
Third time out this year and second fish caught. It was off the point where the old dam used to be.
Caught with a  vibrax spinner while drifting down the river.
Caught on a 1/8 oz underspin with half of a 3 inch Zoom Brush Hog for a trailer. Caught just south of downtown San Antonio at Confluence Park.
Caught on a shiner on a tip up. For fish nerds, it's a native fish commonly found in pools below waterfalls, hence its name.
Fishing for smallmouth down stream from Keystone bridge.
Noah was fishing with his grandpa on a cold and windy June morning.
Caught while jigging a saltwater diamond jig.
Caught this one dangling a jig and minnow on a nice November day on the river. This wasn't the smallmouth I was looking for.

I'm taking claim of a record long held for 42 years. On October 5th I caught a beautiful 17in Cutthroat Trout out of Hidden Lake from Glacier National Park in Montana, not far from where my Dad and Grandpa caught theirs. I caught it on a Mepps Black Fury Spinner while using a $30 collapsible rod and reel I bought from a hardware store on the Blackfeet Indian Reservation. I caught 2 smaller ones earlier in the day before having to head back to meet up with a friend who was picking me up, but I was determined to go back for more. I grabbed my camping gear and backpacked back out to the same lake (3.5 miles away) and spent the night right on the lake where I landed three more Cutthroat. The last one being the biggest at 17in.

Caught on a little green and yellow ice fishing jig with a single red salmon egg. I was fishing in about 25 feet of water through about 18 inches of ice. When he hit, I could tell that it wasn’t a little perch, but he came to the bottom of the hole fairly easily. I saw him swim past the bottom of the hole and he really didn’t want to enter the cylinder. He took line several times and after a few minutes I got his head in the hole. I was afraid to hoist him out with the thin 8 lb test line that had rubbed on the bottom ice edge. I tried to get a finger in a gill with no luck, then I stuck my arm in up to my elbow along side of him and he jumped out of the hole on to the ice. The salmon season doesn’t start until April 1 in NH, so after the picture he went back down the hole.

I caught this 21 inch pickerel at Long Lake in Littleton, MA on 1/16/22 on a tip up with a medium shiner. This came from the historically lucky spot 57 giant steps out and a little bit left of the boat ramp.

34 inches ad 14.8 pounds. Caught off of Gloucester on September 25 in about 80 feet of water on a blue and silver diamond jig. We were fishing in the same spot that Barbara’s previous record was caught. The big ones were biting this day, we boated 4 cod over 30 inches!

Barbara would like to claim the cod record with this 32 inch giant. She caught it on a rig with a 3oz diamond jig and 2 teasers. It bit on one of the Teasers. We were fishing off of Gloucester in about 75 feet of water.

This landlocked Atlantic salmon was 20 inches and 3.2 pounds. It hit a Swedish pimple tipped with a salmon egg at Newfound Lake in New Hampshire. I had just drilled my first hole and dropped the Swedish pimple jig down to see how deep it was. After reaching the bottom 30-40 feet below I was bringing it in to put a tip up in that hole when it felt like I hooked the bottom of the ice. I didn’t think I had brought it up that far and then it started swimming away. It put up a good fight but luckily the 8 pound test line held and I was able to get it through the 18 inches of ice. I didn’t get another bite in 4 more hours of fishing! Fun facts: When the glaciers retreated from New England at the end of the ice age, some rivers were diverted and some salmon were trapped in deep lakes where they were able to survive and reproduce. Newfound Lake did not have a native population and salmon were introduced in 1866. They have developed a successful breeding population by successfully spawning in two feeder creeks. Annnual stocking is done as well.

I'd like to submit the attached picture of a 31 inch cod I caught on 9/12/2020. This guy hit a diamond jig in about 45 feet of water off of Gloucester, MA. The cod were really biting this day. Barbara and I caught at least 30 that morning. Barbara even caught three at once on a diamond jig with two teasers rigged above it!
Caught vertical jigging a KastMaster spoon. This is big for a yellow bass.
Caught about 4 miles off of Rockport in about 130 feet of water on a fluorescent green diamond jig.
Caught about 4 miles off of Rockport in about 130 feet of water on a fluorescent green diamond jig.

The fish finder showed marks near the bottom 27 feet deep. We trolled through there, but our lures weren't getting down that deep. Drifting through the area and vertical jigging a 1/4 oz kastmaster spoon was the ticket.
Barbara pulled this 18 inch beauty up on a Mackeral rig while fishing in about 50 feet of water off the coast of Cape Ann.

Surprised by a rainbow trout when fishing for white bass. Didn't know rainbow trout were in Eagle Creek Reservoir. Later found out that they are stocked in the creek up by Zionsville for put/take fishing. The water gets too warm for them to survive the summer.

Drifting downstream and casting a jig for bluegill near the 82nd street bridge when this strange looking fish hit. It took some expert consultation (thanks Kevin) to identify the species, but I think its correct.
I've caught plenty of these with a cast net for catfish bait, but never hitting a lure. For some reason this one hit a blade bait.
Last weekend I took Kent's family fish record for Cunner. It measured to 14inches and had some nasty looking teeth.

Caught with a blade bait while fishing for wipers below the dam near Martinsville. At first I thought it was an Asian carp with the position of the eye, but Asian carp have small scales. An email to Kevin and his consultation with a rivers fisheries expert confirmed the ID of Bigmouth Buffalo. (Ictiobus cyprinellus)

The pickerel was 19 inches that should be a family record. I got it on a shiner on a tip-up on Superbowl Sunday. How 'bout those Patriots! The line snapped as he was 2/3 of the way out of the hole, so I almost lost this one.
This one was caught on a Christmas tree mackerel rig off of Thatcher island.
Here's Barbara's new family record bonito. It came inat a whopping 8 inches on a Christmas tree mackerel rig in about 50 feet of water off Gloucester mass.
Caught below the dam at Martinsville while attempting to catch some walleye.
The Pollock is 20 inches and was caught off of Gloucester, MA in 60 feet of water on a diamond jig. The Pollock have become more numerous and bigger over the last several years

Caught just downstream from the Broadripple ramp on gold vibrax spinner. The fish finder showed a school of fish and I thought maybe they were crappie. This is the only yellow bass I ever caught in the river.

This Yellowfin Tuna was caught while there was still a mahi mahi flopping on the deck and despite being smaller than any of the mahi mahi, it put up the biggest fight of the day and came out to 33inches.

This Mahi Mahi was the first and biggest of five Mahi Mahi I caught that day aboard the Kiwi Magic Charter Boat. It was caught trolling squid lures at a high speed on a sunny day, and weighed in at 25lbs.

Caught out of Ancarrow's Landing below the I-95 Bridge in downtown Richmond. Slow shad bite this day, only caught six but three were nice american shad. Caught on a hand tied 1/32 oz bucktail jig in red and white on a dropper below a 1/4 oz Shad Dart.

Look what I pulled up from the depths! This squid was cool looking. When I tried to take a selfie with him, he squirted me. When I took the hook out, he instantly changed color to a dark brown then changed back. He was 13 inches. I threw him back since I had no clue how to make calamari.
Caught on Kettle Ledge on a googly eye jig

Caught this on a senko plastic worm with no leader and 10lb test line. I'd been fishing for musky with heavy musky gear, then tried around docks for a bass when this big musky hit. It took two attempts to net as only half the fish would fit in the net.

They are usually only 4 or 5 inches long, so this is a lunker at 12 inches. Caught on a blue diamond jig in 50 feet of water just outside of Gloucester harbor. We didn't catch any good fish this outing. Finley seemed to like his first boat trip.
This colorful little guy bit a piece of squid.
This is a type of puffer fish, caught using squid for bait. He was all puffed up when he first came out of the water, but calmed down by the time the picture was taken.

A whopping white perch that stretched out to 15 inches caught at Long Lake, Littleton, MA. I was out in the canoe with Barbara trolling a chartreuse crankbait with a rattle. Barbara was trolling a wiggly tail chartreuse jig and we were nailing the crappie. Also caught two bass and this surprise white perch.

Mystery little red fish. This guy came up from 70 feet on Kettle ledge off of Gloucester, MA. I have not been able to identify him. He looks just like a copper rockfish, but they only live in the Pacific. He stretched out to 5 1/2 inches but what he lacks in size he makes up for in cuteness. He was caught on a diamond jig with a red tube on the calmest day I've ever seen on the ocean. - Update: Identity determined to be Acadian Redfish.
Ben got this sculpin/sea robin on a googly eye jig also on Kettle Ledge off of Gloucester MA. He was 22 inches long and as ugly as a fish gets
Not the target species!
Caught on a ice jig tipped with bee moth. Cold winter and thick ice.
Caught on an Erie Dearie in the White River near Martinsville, IN
autog, Kent Eliason, 14 inches, October 2013, Gloucester, MA
Barbara smokes Ben's previous Pollock family record. 16 inches caught off of Gloucester, MA
Caught dead drifting a wooly bugger for trout. Thought it was a really good trout till I got a look at him.
Caught while fishing for redfish or sea trout with a popping cork and shrimp.
Hoping for redfish or sea trout, caught with a popping cork and shrimp.

Caught out of Ancarrow's Landing withing 100 yards of the I-95 Bridge in downtown Richmond. Mostly we catch hickory shad, but every now and then an American Shad bites. Caught on a Nunguesser Shad spoon in chartruse and orange.

I was fishing by myself, so you are gonna have to believe the picture. Caught by drifting an 8 inch chunk of eel through the cut-through at Deep Bottom. When she hit, she didn't move, and by drifting the river current was not a factor. The fight seemed to take forever. To get the beast in the boat I put on a glove on one hand while holding the rod in the other. Then grabbed the leader, set down the rod, and put two hands in the mouth to hoist her over the side. Whew. The scale only went to 50 lbs and it topped out. Measurement 44 inches long and 30 inch girth. Using the formula length*girth*girth/800 results in 49.5 lbs.

This was the last fish of a good night of fishing. In total we caught 7 blue cats, 8,21,26,31,33,33,and 42 pounds. Fishing out of Jordan point, all but the 42 pounder were caught in Tar Bay. The 42 came off a hump just off the main river channel. All were caught with fresh cut gizzard shad.
This one was pulling drag before the rod was out of the rod holder.
Emma's herring was caught while jigging for mackeral. Check out the size of the jig compared to the fish.
It was caught on a home-made jig drifting about a mile off of Perkins Cove Maine. We thought the jig was caught on the bottom and turned the boat around to get it unsnagged from the other direction.

Caught on a live bluegill not far downstream from the boat ramp. The weather was hot and the river was low. I let this guy have the bait for a while before putting the reel in gear. When he tightened up on it, he was already across a couple of the other lines. My uncle Eric was with us while visiting, so he got a chance to witness Dad's record fall.
He must have had an attitude since the lure was about 5 inches
Caught on a shad dart in the James River. The shad run up the James every spring to spawn and they get stacked up below the rapids in downtown Richmond.

Caught in 10 foot of water while trying to find a walleye with a small minnow near the bottom. I was using 6lb test line on an ultralight rod, so this guy put up a fight. I thought it was a big catfish the way it stayed down and didn't come the surface until he was wore out.

This was a matter of being in the right place at the right time. I ducked out of work an hour early on Friday and went down to Pony Pasture Park in Richmond to wade for flatheads. This spot is well known for big flatheads and wading is the only practical way to get to it. I've been to this spot 3 times before, but never had action close to this good. In 2 hours I caught 3 flatheads between 20-21 pounds, one 15, and 2 smaller blue cats. I was fishing by myself so this was the best selfie I could manage.

We were all having a nice evening camping on the island and doing pretty well catching catfish. We suspected the gar had been stealing our bait all night, but finally this one got hooked. Their mouths are so thin, and full of bony teeth that they are near impossible to hook.
Kevin grabed the pole as the clicker on the reel screamed. The fish hooked itself on the circle hook, and after that it pulled out drag until it was tired enough to get into the boat.

Nothing like a friend with a nice boat that knows where to go and how to catch big fish! We tried for stripers for awhile by the bay bridge with no luck, then for black drum over by the eastern shore. This fish fought 10 times harder than anthing I've ever had on the end of a line. Every time he would get to the surface near the boat, he'd take off again peeling drag. My arms are still sore two days later. We caught three this day 19, 25, and 34 pounds. We kept the smallest and released the other two.
Only catfish caught this time out. The river had just risen from 1 foot to 4 foot after a few days of heavy rain.

Caught this one on a dead bluegill that we put out when we ran out of live bait. Didn't really expect to catch anything on it but decided to give it a try. Not too much longer the fish was on, and during the fight dad caught a smaller one on another pole.

Caught on a chunk of cut up shad on a circle hook while fishing for blue cats in the Lower James. Luckily was caught during the slack tide so the current wasn't a problem. What a surprise to be expecting a catfish to come up and to see a striper on the end of the line. Had to let this fish go as stripers were not in season at the time.
Caught jigging a diamond jig with a red tube in 75 feet of water on my Birthday.
Caught on small Rapala minnow lure. We weren't quite sure what species this fish was, but some of the locals told us its what they call a Shellcracker. Later correctly identified as a Warmouth Bass.

Check out this striper! It's 37 inches and 15 pounds. We caught it just outside of Gloucester Harbor while trolling a bucktail jig. We saw a lot of bird activity and trolled the area. He hit it hard and then went for the bottom 50 feet below. Catching this one was a group effort. I set the hook and started the fight. Barbara took the helm. The kids cleared the other lines. A friend Mike Bryant took the rod while I grabbed the fish with my new Boga Grip (birthday present). We had one other hit that came off after 3 or 4 minutes. Then Emma was feeling seasick so we headed in to the Annisquam river.

First Cast! This little guy was caught during a 4 day backpacking trip on the first day, first cast. We thought we were in store to catch a lot of in the next few days, but there just weren't many pools that had trout in them, and most we caught were around 6 inches
Caught this monster fly fishing.
Caught while fishing for bluegill with a jig on an ultralight pole. What a fight.

Not much of a fish, but this is only the second spotted bass I've ever caught. Caught on a 7" purple Culprit worm fishing with Laura on a weekend away. Laura caught 27 bluegill. After returning the rental boat we got a call that Travis was in the hospital with an asthma attack and we headed straight for home.

It was caught in the Kennebunk river in Kennebunkport, Maine.  It was mid September and there were millions of small herring like baitfish (?alewives) that the stripers were feeding on.  It was about the middle of the incoming tide and I was using one of my striper streamers.  The stripers had been herding the baitfish and pigging out on them the day before.  Now, the baitfish were scattered and there was an occasional splash as a striper got one.  I cast across the current and after 5 or 6 strips of line, WHAM!  The fish quickly took the rest of the slack line and the reel spun as he made his first run.Unfortunately, I didn't get my hand switched to the reel quick enough and the line tangled on the reel as it spun out of control.  Now I could not give him line and the line was so tight that I couldn't get it untangled quickly.  I started to follow the fish to ease the pressure on the line which thankfully was a strong 15 lb test tippet.  Luckily the water was not to deep and I was able to follow him for about 50 yards.  After about 5 minutes I was able to gain a bit of line and move back towards shore.  A couple of minutes later, the battle was over.
Caught on 1/32 oz jig in 6 feet of water.
Caught on 1/32 oz jig in 6 feet of water.

This fish was caught on a Purple Culprit plastic worm and judging from the worn off tail, it was on the spawning bed. Caught at 6:30 AM on a cool Sunday morning and released after the picture and weight on a digital scale.  Travis netted the fish and we caught 8 other bass that morning in 3 hours of fishing.

While staying at Emery's cottoges on the shore of Frenchman's bay near Bar Harbor Maine, we discovered that mackeral will hit streamers and spinners trolled from a canoe.  We caught a bunch.  Ben's was the biggest at 11 inches, and was caught trolling one of Kent's black ghost streamers.
Caught on a minnow after saying "one more cast". That is one ugly fish.

Travis caught this ugly thing on peanut butter dough bait after about 10 minutes of fishing. He was using his dad's pole, his dad's bait, and his dad grabbed the fish. His dad isn't at all bitter about Travis catching the fish instead of him.
Caught on a minnow on Friday the 13th, which was also Good Friday. This fish was released to grow some more.
Caught on fly rod with self tied fly.
Caught on a minnow and a hook by the boy in the floppy hat.

Travis was 8 years old when he caught this fish while on a walleye charter on Lake Erie. After a hard fight, I was disappointed to see a drum instead of a nice walleye, but Travis didn't care. All the fish caught that day were on an Erie Dearies on a bottom bouncing rig. The waves were big that day and we all got seasick.

We caught several nice yellow perch during a week long trip to Tall Pines camp near Dryden, Ontario. The largest perch ran 13 and 14 inches. They sure were good eating, and it was hard to chase walleye when the perch were biting.
Caught while fishing for bluegill with a jig on an ultralight pole. What a fight.

This fish was caught on a Manns Manipulator plastic worm cast under a dock on a hot summer afternoon. Kevin helped reel the fish in, so he gets credit for this one. The fish was released after the picture was taken. This picture was also sent in to the "Big Ol' Fish" contest at channel 6 and was aired on Indianapolis TV during Ed Sorenson's sports.
Trumpet Fish, Kent Eliason, Long and Skinny, March 1994, Pacific Ocean, Maui, Hawaii

I hooked this bluefish while casting a surface plug from the jetty at the mouth of the Kennebunkport river. I had lost a big one a few minutes earlier when the snap swivel gave way. I frantically tied on a new one as it was obvious from the bird and baitfish activity that there was a school of blues feeding. By the time I got the new plug tied on, the activity had stopped. I was lamenting my bad luck when this fish hit. The fish put up a tough fight taking out about 100 yards of line. After about 20 minutes I managed to get my hand around its tail and hand it out of the water.

This bass was caught on my first trip to Canada. We were staying at a camp on Lake Ena, and had made the run up Corn Creek to Corn Lake. I was fishing with a black jitterbug when the fish hit HARD. It put up a strong fight jumping twice. Dan Goff netted the fish for me and while removing the fish from the net, the fish inserted one of the hooks deep into Dan's thumb. After some painfull manipulations, the hook was out of Dan's thumb and the fish was in the cooler.
This fish was caught on a pixie spoon the same day as the big King salmon.

This fish ranks as the largest of any species I have caught so far (as of 1998). I hooked it on a pixie spoon which is a hammered silver spoon with a plastic flourescent orange insert. It took about 45 minutes to land this giant. At one point he sat on the far side of the creek and I could not budge him, so I picked up a rock an threw it over at him to get him to move to my side of the stream. That attempt made him move farther downstream which was not good. The current was much faster farther downstream, and I never would have landed him if he had chosen to go another 20 yards further. Eventually he yielded to the pressure and I was able to grab him by the gills and hall him out of the water for this picture. Note: my girlfriend (now my wife) Barbara landed a 25 pounder from the same spot.
No Details

I caught this grayling in a little stream that crossed the road that runs along the Alaskan pipeline near the arctic circle. I had walked about a mile along the stream and came to a pool with a log across it. I cast a silver spinner to the log and as soon as I started the retrive, five grayling came out from under the log. One of the largest ones hit the spinner and measured 18 inches. I also caught a 14 inch and 15 inch graylings from under the same log.
I caught this dolly varden trout while casting a Krocodile spoon parallel to the shore in the Chilkoot inlet of the Pacific Ocean.
This fish was caught on a pixie spoon.

Caught while on a charter 'Lucky Pierre' out of Homer, Alaska. Someone on a boat near us caught a halibut that broke 100 pounds. The captain of that boat shot the fish in the head before bringing it aboard so it wouldn't hurt anyone. Note: halibut over 300 pounds have been caught in these waters.

I caught this pink salmon while casting a Krocodile spoon from a dock on the Chilkoot Inlet of the Pacific Ocean near Hains, Alaska. This salmon must have jumped 10 times and I nearly lost it when it darted underneath the dock I was standing on and got the line tangled. My dad took time out from his eagle and killer whale watching to help me get the line untangled. I was truly lucky to land this one!
I caught this brown trout with a snagging hook (legally) in the Pike River on the campus at Carthage College.

I caught this Chinook Salmon when I was a junior at Carthage College. I was using a snagging hook (legally) in the Pike river which runs through the campus. The rugby team was practicing nearby and when I hooked it they all came over to watch the action. The rod and reel I was using were not suited to this size of fish. There was only about 30 yards of 12 pound test line on the reel so I had to follow the fish along the bank of the river. It jumped clear out of the water twice and finally after about 20 minutes, my roommate Tom Lake waded in and netted it.
This record is held jointly by myself and my Dad. This fish is one of several this size that were caught using a #4 mepps spinner and casting across the current near likely holding spots.
This record is held jointly by myself and my Dad. This fish is one of several this size that were caught using a #4 mepps spinner and casting across the current near likely holding spots.

This northern pike was the first big fish I had ever caught. I was casting a large black and white spoon and retrieving it slowly when it just stopped. After a spectacular fight with a couple of tail walking jumps, my brother Karl slid the net under it. I was so excited I did not throw another cast all evening. My brother Karl on the other hand, threw a black and white spoon frantically the rest of the evening!
